title: Expected square of a noised one-bit function
statement:
Let $f\colon\{0,1\}^1\to\bbr$ be a Boolean function of arity one, and let $\rho$ be any
real number. Define $T_\rho$ by multiplying the Fourier coefficient at each subset
$S$ of the coordinate set by $\rho^{|S|}$; then its expected square under the uniform
measure is
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big] \;=\; \hat f(\emptyset)^2 \;+\; \rho^2\,\hat f(\{0\})^2,
\]
where $\emptyset$ and $\{0\}$ are the only two frequencies for a single coordinate.
hypotheses_covered: f is a Boolean function of arity 1
ρ is an arbitrary real number
replaced:
For a one-bit function $f$ and noise rate $\rho$,
\[
  \E\big[(T_\rho f)^2\big] = \widehat{f}(\emptyset)^2 + \rho^2\,\widehat{f}(\{0\})^2 .
\]
